title: Accessory detach on death — accessories become independent Rapier rigid bodies, scatter + fall separately from the main ragdoll
intent: After ragdoll death (shipped S129-S137), the bomber's body parts become Rapier rigid bodies that tumble realistically. But accessories — antennae, visor, backpack, cap, fins (shipped S106) — currently INHERIT their parent body's motion because they're parented to the mount-socket pivots on the body's child hierarchy. Result: they ride along with the torso/head ragdoll, no independent motion. This story makes them DETACH on death: each accessory entity becomes its own Rapier rigid body with its own mass, shape, scatter impulse, and lifetime. Antennae fly up + random; fins scatter horizontally; backpack pops opposite-to-blast; cap launches straight up with spin; visor falls quickly. Adds the 'stuff explodes off' beat that ragdoll lacks today. Lifetime exceeds the main ragdoll's 0.6s — accessories keep tumbling 1.5s, fading out, then despawn. Engine-side extension to the ragdoll module + Kaboom Crew template update.
rationale: Source: user feedback 2026-05-27: 'аксессуары откреплялись и отдельно падали при смерти'. Natural extension of two shipped tracks — accessory layer (S106 GDP-026-003 / 026-005) and ragdoll engine module (S126-S128 + S129-S137 GDP-024-001/002). The current behaviour (accessories ride the body) is the lazy default; detach makes the death moment a multi-object spectacle in line with the modern-arcade slapstick tone (Boomerang Fu / Bombergrounds: Reborn). Pure presentation — zero gameplay impact, accessories already gameplay-irrelevant after collect. Implementation: tiny engine extension + per-accessory template config in the kaboom-bomber template.
acceptanceHints: Depends on: ragdoll module (engine/physics/ragdoll/) SHIPPED S126-S128. Accessory layer SHIPPED S106. Kaboom-bomber template + first consumer SHIPPED S129-S137.
ENGINE EXTENSION (engine/physics/ragdoll/):
RagdollTemplate schema gains optional `accessoryBodies?: Record<string, AccessoryBodyDef>`. The key is the accessory NAME ('antennae', 'visor', 'backpack', 'cap', 'fins' for Kaboom). Value:
AccessoryBodyDef {
shape: 'box' | 'capsule' | 'sphere' (default 'box')
dimensions: [number, number, number]    // shape-dependent — see RagdollBodyDef §3.1
mass: number                            // relative; default 0.02 (light)
linearDamping?: number                  // default 0.3 (drifts further than body)
angularDamping?: number                 // default 0.4 (tumbles more)
scatterImpulse: {
verticalBias: number                  // +y bias (positive = up). Default 1.2 for light accessories, 0.0 for heavy
horizontalSpread: number              // random ± radians around blast direction. Default 0.6
bombDirectionalBias: number           // -1..1 — negative = away from blast (backpack/cap), positive = with blast
speedMagnitude: number                // base velocity in cell/sec; default 2.0
lifetimeMs?: number                     // default 1500 (longer than main 0.6s ragdoll)
collisionGroup?: 'RAGDOLL_BODY' | 'ACCESSORY_DEBRIS'    // default ACCESSORY_DEBRIS (passes through ragdoll body; collides with arena floor + walls only)

RagdollSpawnSystem (existing) gains a new step: BEFORE spawning the main body rigid bodies, query all accessory entities tagged with SkeletalBinding (or whichever marker the accessory builders use to identify accessory meshes — verify from S106 implementation).
For each accessory entity:
1. Look up its accessory name in template.accessoryBodies. If missing, skip (the accessory rides the body — current behaviour, fallback).
2. RE-PARENT the accessory mesh from its mount-socket pivot to the new accessory body entity (so when the body moves, the mesh follows).
3. Spawn a Rapier rigid body at the accessory's CURRENT world position (just like the main ragdoll preserves the pre-death pose).

4. Compute scatter impulse vector: blast_direction × bombDirectionalBias + worldUp × verticalBias + (random in horizontalSpread cone), all scaled by speedMagnitude. Determinism: derive the random component from (bomber entity id + accessory name) hash — same death + same accessory = identical scatter direction.
5. Apply impulse to the new rigid body.
6. Write an AccessoryDebris component on the new entity: { despawnAt: now + lifetimeMs, fadeStart: now + lifetimeMs - 300 }.
RagdollSyncSystem (existing) extends to also sync AccessoryDebris entities' Transforms from Rapier.

RagdollTeardownSystem (existing) extends — on accessory's despawnAt timer, dispose its Rapier body + entity. Optional fadeStart 300ms before despawn applies a tween reducing the mesh opacity to 0 for smooth disappearance.
COLLISION:

Accessory debris uses 'ACCESSORY_DEBRIS' collision group by default. Excludes collisions with: ragdoll body parts (no double-hit physics), other accessory debris (cheap; no inter-debris collisions), bombs (passes through), pickups (passes through), live bombers (passes through). Includes collisions with: ARENA_WALL + ARENA_FLOOR.
Project can override via template — e.g. backpack collides with everything for extra weight feel.
KABOOM-BOMBER TEMPLATE EXTENSION (examples/kaboom-crew/src/characters/kaboom-bomber-ragdoll-template.ts):
Extend the existing template with accessoryBodies section. Tuned per accessory:

ANTENNAE — shape: capsule [0.02, 0.10, 0.02], mass: 0.01 (very light), linearDamping: 0.2, scatterImpulse: { verticalBias: 1.8, horizontalSpread: 1.0, bombDirectionalBias: 0.2, speedMagnitude: 2.5 }. Fly up + random direction.

VISOR — shape: box [0.18, 0.04, 0.02], mass: 0.04, linearDamping: 0.5 (falls fast), scatterImpulse: { verticalBias: 0.2, horizontalSpread: 0.4, bombDirectionalBias: 0.1, speedMagnitude: 1.5 }. Falls quickly with mild scatter.

BACKPACK — shape: box [0.30, 0.28, 0.12], mass: 0.10 (heavy), linearDamping: 0.4, scatterImpulse: { verticalBias: 0.6, horizontalSpread: 0.3, bombDirectionalBias: -0.8, speedMagnitude: 2.2 }. Pops opposite-to-blast — backpack flies AWAY from the blast like trying to escape.

CAP — shape: capsule [0.08, 0.06, 0.08], mass: 0.03, linearDamping: 0.3, scatterImpulse: { verticalBias: 2.0, horizontalSpread: 0.4, bombDirectionalBias: 0.0, speedMagnitude: 2.8 }. Pops straight up with spin (high angularDamping for slow tumble).

FINS — shape: box [0.20, 0.24, 0.02], mass: 0.025, linearDamping: 0.35, scatterImpulse: { verticalBias: 0.3, horizontalSpread: 1.2, bombDirectionalBias: 0.3, speedMagnitude: 2.0 }. Horizontal scatter (lateral wings — flap-fall feel).
Lifetime: 1500ms for all accessories. Tune in playtest.

CHAIN-REACTION EDGE: bomber killed by multiple simultaneous blasts → impulse direction is averaged (per the main ragdoll's existing magnitude clamp at 1.8). Same averaged direction feeds the accessory scatter base direction.

SELF-BOMB EDGE: bomber killed by own bomb (blast origin = bomber's cell, no direction) → accessories use pure verticalBias + horizontalSpread without bombDirectionalBias contribution. Result: 'pop' in random directions.
VISUAL:

Accessories tagged 'soft-attached' (antennae + fins from S106) — their spring-sway system stops touching them once they become independent rigid bodies (the system query already filters on having a parent pivot; after detach, no parent pivot → spring-sway skips).
Optional 0.3s fade-out via opacity tween before despawn (per the AccessoryDebris.fadeStart field). Reusable Tween primitive.
AUDIO:
No new event in v1. The existing death audio already fires on bomber's alive-flip; adding accessory-impact sounds is per-collision audio (very expensive — defer).
Future polish: when an accessory hits the floor (Rapier collision callback), play a tiny 'thud' / 'click' sound. Punt to playtest if the silent fall feels lifeless.
MULTIPLAYER (per ragdoll module's existing client-side-presentation rule, gameplay-systems.md §12.1):
Server tells 'bomber X died with blast Y'. Client runs LOCAL accessory detach with local Rapier sim. Tabs may see slightly different scatter trajectories (floating-point drift) — acceptable.
Server does NOT simulate accessory physics. Saves server CPU.
DETERMINISM:
Per-accessory random scatter component derives from (bomber entity id + accessory name + frame number) hash. Same input → identical scatter. Replay fixture continues to be reproducible.
Bot-vs-bot regression test passes (gameplay state unaffected; visual replay may differ but gameplay-deterministic).
PERFORMANCE:

Per-bomber accessory bodies: up to 3 (S106 caps accessory pool at 3 per bomber). 4 bombers × 3 = 12 extra Rapier bodies during death window (1.5s). Plus main 10-body ragdoll × 4 = 40. Total worst case 52 bodies. Well under physics-bench's 200-body benchmark.
ACCESSORY_DEBRIS collision group narrows interactions; sim cost is dominated by simple gravity + a few wall-collisions.
UNIT TESTS:
Death → for each accessory on the bomber, an AccessoryDebris entity spawns with the configured shape + mass.
Accessory mesh re-parented from mount socket → accessory-debris-entity. Original mount socket pivot's child set decremented.
Scatter direction determinism: same (entity id, accessory name) → identical scatter vector across two test runs.
Lifetime: AccessoryDebris entity despawned after lifetimeMs. fadeStart applies opacity tween 300ms before despawn.
Collision group: accessory debris doesn't push the main ragdoll (test verifies main body's Transform unaffected by accessory body collisions).
Self-bomb edge: blast origin = bomber's cell → accessory scatter uses verticalBias + spread only (no directional bias).
VISUAL QA (manual):
Trigger a kill from the east on a bomber with antennae + visor + cap → see antennae fly up + east; visor fall quickly with mild east-ish scatter; cap pop straight up with spin.
Backpack-equipped bomber killed from the east → backpack flies west (opposite-to-blast).
4 bombers all die in a chain reaction → ~12 accessory debris bodies all visible bouncing; arena stays uncluttered after lifetime expires (1.5s).
OUT OF SCOPE:
Per-accessory audio on floor-hit (defer to playtest signal).
Accessories that interact with gameplay (e.g. a flying backpack bumps a bomb's cell, triggering chain-react). Out — accessory debris is presentation only, no gameplay collision groups.
Player-pickup of dropped accessories (collect a dead opponent's antennae for your own bomber). Out — entirely cosmetic-flow change, contradicts the locked cosmetic-unlock pipeline.
Custom per-recipe-seed scatter (e.g. specific seeds make accessories scatter differently). The scatter is template-driven; seed only affects the random hash component.
Accessory ground-collision callbacks for VFX (sparkle on landing). Stretch polish; punt.
Reverse handover (accessory re-attaching to body if bomber revives). No revive in Kaboom Crew.
